item.title: Inconsistent behavior re: editing files vs spitting code in chat

labels.name: info-needed
labels.description: Issue requires more information from poster

item.body:
Type: Bug I started a chat with @workspace in the Chat interface to get project context, then move the conversation to Edits. My previous attempt was stared in Edits and it kept hallucinating instead of reading my code, but at least it was editing the files in the editor. This new conversation, it refuses to actually edit any files, and even though it's in Edits mode, not Chat mode, it's still only putting the file contents in the chat and won't actually edit. comments.body:
This keeps happening every day I use it and the failure cases are slightly different from model to model, but I've been focusing on Claude. I think there are bugs with the working set and also with the way it tries to normalize filepaths. I've been doing a lot of experiments asking Claude how it is trying to represent the file markers and paths, and getting it to show me stuff like the `` header and `// filepath: ` syntax it puts with the code that VSCode intends to trap for the editor. Occasionally it will start with a markdown filepath heading like: ``` # /c:/Users/vandersen/source/repos/file.js ``` Then it will encode it as a file URL to get through to the VSCode editor layer, but it will grab the `# ` too: ``` file:///#%20%2Fc%3A%2FUsers%2Fvandersen%2Fsource%2Frepos%2Ffile.js) ``` Sometimes it will mess up a file in a way that doesn't cause a blue link or a file diff pill to show up at all, sometimes it will mangle them so they show up but they never get edited (this is probably the failure case related to the working set being full), and sometimes it will mangle them so VSCode doesn't know which folder to put it in, throws up a file open dialog, and then no matter what you type in there usually ends up just shitting files to the C:\ root instead of your workspace. In cases like this, you can hover over the link or right-click and copy the unfiltered chat message, and see what file path it's using. Sometimes you can easily spot the error and just tell it to rephrase. I've done a lot of "show me just the headers of the last 10 files you sent" or "x.js file worked for me but y.md" did not. Can you spot any differences between how you tried to create those two files?" One of the best advices so far has been to always issue an absolute path before a series of relative ones. Another great one is to make sure to use 4 backticks whenever sending markdown, not 3. Then it can nest code blocks and chat output doesn't break the file scanning algo. My best results have been adding various prescriptions to .github/copilot-instructions.md once I have proven in a chat session that they improve the contents. Here are some of the most successful so far: .github/copilot-instructions.md 
Before creating multiple new files or edits at once:
1. Present a file tree of the new or chaned files with # right margin comments to indicate the purpose of the file or change.
2. There are many failure cases which can happen if you try to send files before properly discussing and normalizing file paths.
3. You may discuss paths relative to the project for expedience, but all actual file edits or proposals should include the full path.
4. When writing markdown blocks, always use at least 4 backticks to allow for embedded 3-backtick fenced code blocks within the markdown.

:: Key success pattern for creating new files or edits in Markdown ::


````markdown
// filepath: /absolute/path/to/file.md
Content here
```code
including fenced content
```
````


:: Note the 4 backticks to allow for embedded 3-backtick code blocks within the markdown ::


```other-code-types
// filepath: /absolute/path/to/file.ext
Content here which does not need fenced code blocks
```

Please try this again. A lot of work has gone into chat and we also have to better models.

When still seeing this, use the Debug view and please share the request log (F1 > Open View > Chat Debug).

This issue has been closed as it has been labeled with `info-needed` and has not received the additional information that was requested from the issue author. It has been labeled as `info-needed` for 7 days.
